current-induced torques with Dresselhus symmetry are observed in heterostructures with TaTe2 and that the dominant mechanism of the Dresselhaus component of the torque is not a spin orbit torque, but is instead the Oersted magnetic field arising from a current component that flows perpendicular to an applied voltage due to the resistance anisotrophy of the TaTe2 material.

current-induced torque measurements in Py/TaTe2 heterostructures are consistent with a combination of the spin-orbit torque and the torque due to a current component flowing perpendicular to the applied bias voltage.

the current-induced torques measured in Py/TaTe2 are due to a combination of spin-orbit torque and a current-induced field arising from a transverse component of the current that flows perpendicular through the TaTe2 layer.

current-induced torques with Dresselhau symmetry can arise from the Oersted fields of the transverse current in heterostructures incorporating materials with resistance anisotrpoies and low crystal symmetrie.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we report a new mechanism of current-induced torquese in Py/TaTe2 heterostructures.
we have shown that a current flowing perpendicular to a material’s resistance anisotropies produces an Oersted field that can induce a torque with Dresselhaus-like symmetry.
the current-induced torques observed in our experiments are not spin-orbit torques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
current flow perpendicular to the applied current is not always negligible, as is usually assumed in models for current-induced torques.
the current flow pattern in any given heterostructure is a critical consideration in interpreting the results of experiments that probe spin-orbit torques.
the presence of a Dresselhaus component of the current-induced torques does not necessarily mean that spin-orbit coupling is present.
